# dsh-session-bridge

Let a DeepSeek Harness agent open
**foreground** sessions, drive them, and read the result back — an

d hand out the
authenticated URL of the local web app.
## Why

The Host already has everything needed: `ctx.sessionController` can create, prompt,
inspect and canc

el a session, and `ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl()` returns the
web app URL carrying a launch toke
n. None of it is reachable from a model tool.

Without this plugin, an agent that wants to verify something in a real foreground
session has to:

1. dig a `dsh-auth-*` cookie out of Chromium's cookie store — and guess which one
matches the curren

t port, because the token encodes `authority: 127.0.0.1:<port>`;
2. reverse-engineer the `/api/*` RP

C envelope and its `_request` argument shape;
3. poke the DOM to get text into the composer, then re
ad the rendered transcript.
Each of those is one tool call here.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `dsh_web_url` | The local web GUI URL. Masks the launch token by default; pass `includeToken: true

` to get a browser-usable URL (requires the `danger-full-access` preset). |
| `dsh_session_create` |

Create a foreground session. Returns its id. |
| `dsh_session_prompt` | Send a prompt to a session

(`queue` or `steer`). |
| `dsh_session_read` | Read a session's transcript. `waitMs` waits for the c

urrent turn to finish. |
| `dsh_session_cancel` | Cancel a session's running turn. |
### Token handling in `dsh_web_url`

The launch token minted by `connection.authenticatedUrl()` is a live credential:
any browser that op

ens the URL gets an authenticated session. A tool result also
lands in the conversation transcript,

and from there into logs, exports and any
copy of the chat.

So the default is `maskToken`: the tool returns `origin` plus a URL whose token is
reduced to its fi

rst and last four characters. Pass `includeToken: true` only when
something actually needs to open a
browser, and do not persist or paste the result.

**`includeToken: true` is gated on the caller's permission preset.** The tool asks
the `permissionPr

esets` service for the calling session's preset
(`current(session)`) and resolves it to `{ sandbox,

approval }`. The plain token is
only handed out when `sandbox === "danger-full-access"`; every other

preset gets
`insufficient-permission` plus the masked URL instead.

The gate fails closed. If `permissionPresets` is missing (older or headless
deployments), if `curren

t()` returns `custom` that `resolve()` cannot handle, if
either call throws, or if `execution.agent.

session` is unavailable, the answer is
"no token" — never "allow".

`lib/format.js` holds the pure functions (`maskToken`, `clip`, `reasonLabel`,
`transcribe`, `waitFor

Turn`); it imports nothing from the Host, so the suite runs
on plain Node 20 with no dependencies. `

test/web-url.test.mjs` wires a fake `ctx`
through `apply()` to cover the permission gate, including

all the fail-closed
paths.
## Foreground vs delegated

This is the part that matters. A **foreground** session is a root agent: it has
the `userQuestions`

service, so a plugin that needs human consent can actually
ask. A **delegated** task (a subagent, a
workflow agent) does not, and gets:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

So plugins like dsh-cua-macos can only
be exercised end to end from a foreground session — which is

exactly what these
tools create.

Restart DSH afterwards. The plugin has no dependencies.

## Notes

- `dsh_session_read` truncates long text and returns at most `maxMessages`
messages (default 40). Re

ad a long session in pieces.
- The transcript includes tool calls and their results, so a session th

at used
other tools is still auditable from here.
- `dsh_web_url` needs the `webApp` service; a head

less deployment has none and
the tool says so instead of failing.
